subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: The Pentium FDIV Bug
description: A quick, practical guide to The Pentium FDIV Bug.

hook.text: Intel's brand-new Pentium chip gave wrong answers to certain division problems. It shipped in millions of PCs.

buildup.text: In 1994 a math professor discovered the Pentium processor returned incorrect floating-point division results.

discovery.text: A lookup table used in the division algorithm had five missing entries out of 1,066. Tiny gap, big consequences.

twist.text: Intel initially dismissed it as rare. Public outrage forced a $475 million recall—the largest chip recall ever.

climax.text: The Pentium FDIV bug taught hardware and software makers: never dismiss a defect just because it's 'rare.'

punchline.text: Five missing table entries cost Intel $475 million.

quiz.question: What caused the Pentium FDIV bug?
options: Five missing entries in a lookup table
